name: Kigurumi body-shaping add-ons

card.summary: Breast forms, binders and hip padding worn under a bodysuit so a kigurumi performer's body matches the proportions of the character being portrayed.
card.note: Compression garments can restrict breathing and cause overheating in prolonged wear.

quick.overview:
Kigurumi (animegao) is a masked cosplay style in which a performer wears a molded mask with a flesh-toned bodysuit. Padding and breast forms under the suit shape the body to the character.[1]

The payoff is a silhouette that matches the character's illustrated figure, with curves or slimmer lines created under the suit rather than by the body itself.
quick.how: Performers layer padding, breast forms or binders and hip pads beneath a skin-tight nylon/spandex zentai-style suit, then add the mask.[1][2]
quick.risks: No clinical studies exist. As with any tight garments or padding worn for long periods, discomfort and heat build-up are common concerns; guidance comes from the community rather than research.

lead: Kigurumi, also called animegao, is a masked form of cosplay that began in official Japanese anime stage shows and was later taken up by hobbyists. Performers wear a plastic mask and a flesh-toned bodysuit, with padding and breast forms beneath the suit to match the character's body shape.[1]

Most characters portrayed are female, though male, mechanical, elfin and demonic characters appear.[1] The skin-tight suit is a zentai-type garment, typically nylon/spandex, which holds the add-ons in place.[2]

angle.text: The add-ons change the visible outline of the torso and hips for the duration of wear, letting performers match a character's build.

paras: Padding and breast forms are worn under the suit to match the character's body shape.[1] The suit is a zentai-type full-body garment, commonly made from nylon/spandex blends.[2]
